reviews.title: Peak cooling, easy installation
reviews.comment: The EK Nucleus AIO CR360 Lux D-RGB All-in-One Liquid CPU Cooler is an absolute gem, surpassing all my expectations and setting new standards for cooling performance. From its sleek design to its exceptional cooling capabilities, this liquid CPU cooler delivers an unparalleled cooling solution that is a must-have for any PC enthusiast or overclocking aficionado. First and foremost, the installation process was a breeze, thanks to the user-friendly design of the EK Nucleus AIO. With clearly labeled components and a comprehensive installation manual, I had the cooler up and running in no time, even as a first-time liquid cooling user. The cooling performance is where this AIO liquid cooler truly shines. The powerful 360mm radiator, combined with high-quality fans and a robust water pump, efficiently dissipates heat from my CPU, keeping temperatures well under control even during the most demanding gaming or rendering sessions. Say goodbye to overheating worries, as the EK Nucleus AIO CR360 Lux D-RGB ensures that my CPU stays cool and stable, allowing for optimal performance without any thermal throttling. The D-RGB lighting is a visual delight, adding a touch of elegance to my PC build. The lighting effects can be easily customized and synchronized with other D-RGB components, creating a stunning light show that enhances the overall aesthetics of my rig. Whether you prefer a subtle glow or a vibrant display, the EK Nucleus AIO delivers a customizable and eye-catching lighting experience. What truly sets this liquid CPU cooler apart is its whisper-quiet operation. Even under heavy loads, the EK Nucleus AIO remains impressively silent, allowing me to immerse myself in my work or gaming without any distracting noise. This feature is a game-changer for those seeking both top-notch cooling performance and a peaceful computing environment. Furthermore, EK's commitment to quality is evident in the durable construction of the AIO cooler. The materials used are of premium quality, and the build feels solid and reliable, giving me peace of mind that my CPU is in safe hands. In conclusion, the EK Nucleus AIO CR360 Lux D-RGB All-in-One Liquid CPU Cooler is an outstanding addition to any high-performance PC build. Its cooling prowess, ease of installation, customizable lighting, and silent operation make it a standout product in the AIO liquid cooling market. If you're looking for the ultimate cooling solution that blends performance and aesthetics seamlessly, look no further than the EK Nucleus AIO CR360 Lux D-RGB Liquid CPU Cooler. It has undoubtedly exceeded my expectations and solidified its place as an indispensable component in my rig.
reviews.author: Tavis

reviews.title: Quality Construction All Around
reviews.comment: Paired this with a Ryzen 7950X on an Asus x670e Extreme board in a Phanteks Enthoo Pro case (PH-ES614PTG_BK). It is a tight fit, but I did manage to get it in and also keep the built-in control bay with the flip cover too without modification. I was also able to load up my three other front 5.25 bays too, although I had to place the shallowest one at the top and then also dremel the 3.5->5.25 bay adapter a bit in order to get it to fit comfortably in front of the CR360. Due to the mounting positions on the Enthoo case the radiator sits a bit further forward, but looking down from the top it is actually perfectly centered in the top dust filter cutout. I decided to mount the pump with lines on the bottom to minimize the stress and tension on the lines due to the positioning of the radiator with respect to the mobo. The top pump display is magnetic and can be rotated in a matter of seconds. Build Quality: This thing just oozes quality, especially the radiator. Clean, sturdy, no cheap plastic anywhere. Everything impressed me from the overall packaging to even the quality of the manual! Installation: Very straight forward once you determine the bracket and standoffs with the correct threads. The pump already has thermal paste evenly applied. Wiring is a breeze and their daisy chain system makes cable management a little less painful. Some others mentioned the top radiator threads were not cut 100% properly and they either had a hard time getting them started or had to break out a tap and die set to clean them up, but I did not have this issue. All screws and bolts threaded in without issue first attempt. Performance: Extremely quiet at idle (speeds under 30%). At 100% the fans are quite loud (like jet engine loud), but with this cooler (and no PBO!) I haven't gone beyond 80 degrees yet at stock. While doing normal tasks the fans range from 30%-60% based on my curves, and it does become noticeable, but it's still quieter than my old AM3 system with a single fan Corsair AIO! I have not yet benchmarked or stress tested my system as it's not fully complete yet, but I feel confident with my choice in this cooler. Oh, and I haven't had time to play with ARGB in Aura yet for any of my components, so the review picture attached shows the default rainbow pattern for everything. That said, the LED brightness and diffusion look to be spot on.
reviews.author: mkinpa

reviews.title: Cooling my 9950X3D with no noise!
reviews.comment: Fantastic aio!  I didn't know this one existed.  Was looking for something to run on linux with no LCD.  Kept getting the usual Arctic LF III suggestions, but not only was that thing massive but just a pain to mess with.  Gambled on the EK aio and it's been amazing.  Can't hear the pump on full speed at all and my 9950X3D temps idle around 41 and so far haven't climbed over 60's while gaming.  Did throw some Noctua fans on it, but I really cant tell the difference with the included fans. Was easy to use with openrgb, just assigned 12 leds and thats it.  Definitely recommend!  Not sure why this thing gets overlooked.  If you just go by Youtube and Reddit, all that exists is the Arctic, lol.
reviews.author: Jonny Quest

reviews.title: EKWB Delivers a Great AIO
reviews.comment: EKWB has been making top-notch water-cooling components for years. After upgrading my CPU and motherboard, I chose to go with an AIO unit instead of building another dedicated water-cooling loop. Since my old loop used EKWB plates and components, I trusted they dotted their i's and crossed their t's when it comes to their own AIO unit. I have gotten nothing but great performance with it cooling my i9-14900KF. The kit was very easy to install, and the instructions were clear to understand. The hardest part might be hiding the fan cables, and that's not too hard (although I messed that up). I like the fan design, I had been using EKWB Vardar fans, these new ones are touted as an improved iteration. The RGB is pretty bright and the animations are smooth, although after taking a few pictures, I just put it in stealth mode. I use my CPU for rendering a good portion of the time with Houdini's Karma CPU engine and it's able to handle multi hour renders without any hiccups or changes in clock speed. It may not cool quite as well as a dedicated dual radiator loop; but if you don't want to spend a good chunk on fittings, tubes, plates, radiators, etc. (or fuss with putting it together) then this AIO is a perfect option.
reviews.author: Chopped

reviews.title: Great performance. Loud fan ramps.
reviews.comment: I really like this AIO. It works very well keeping the CPU cool and that is by far the most important aspect of it. That said, I have just a couple gripes with the AIO. First, the fan noise is not great. It really ramps up the noise when your CPU starts doing things. Setting some custom fan curves to keep it from going up and down too often is very important to make this noise manageable. My only other real complaint is also a positive, that the RGB and is purely motherboard controlled. There is no such thing as a RGB suite that actually works well, and USB controlled fan hubs are often a far bigger headache. Unfortunately for me, Gigabyte motherboards are really stupid about what RGB fusion and what their new control center can actually configure, so it's been a bit annoying to get the colors sticking around on anything going through the motherboard. Just keep that in mind. I would still recommend this product.
